+# Toner
+
+### Improving Muon and AdamW with input geometry
+
+Toner uses each layer’s input statistics to precondition its weight update.
+Use **MuonT** with Muon or **AdamT** with AdamW, through either the general
+PyTorch implementation or the asynchronous CUDA backend.
+
+[Read the blog](https://muon-sfd-half-eighth-amin-1105.leamin.chatgpt.site/)
+· [Training example](examples/train_nanogpt.py)
+· [Fast CUDA guide](docs/FAST.md)
+
+## Quick start
+
+```bash
+git clone https://github.com/mohamad-amin/Toner.git
+cd Toner
+pip install -e '.[examples,fast]'
+
+python examples/prepare_text.py
+python examples/train_nanogpt.py --optimizer muon --backend fast
+```
+
+This trains the included modded-nanoGPT model on Shakespeare, reports training
+and validation loss, and saves a checkpoint. Use `--optimizer adam` for AdamT.
+The model has separate Q/K/V projections, rotary attention, and a squared-ReLU MLP.
+
+For your own text, pass `--input corpus.txt` to `prepare_text.py`. Prepared
+uint16 token files are also supported through `--data-dir` and `--vocab-size`.
+Set the matrix and auxiliary learning rates directly with `--lr` and `--aux-lr`.
+
+## Reproduce a comparison
+
+The [nanoGPT reproduction guide](reproduce/nanogpt/README.md) provides loadable
+Muon/MuonT configurations at **128K, 512K, 1M and 2M** tokens per update, pinned
+data shards, and four-GPU training commands.
+
+The [Marin reproduction guide](reproduce/marin/README.md) provides the Figure 1
+configurations for **130M, 300M, 520M and 1.2B models** at their 1× training
+budgets, with data preparation and an eight-GPU PyTorch runner. The two native
+Marin baselines retain separate JAX configurations.
+
+## Choose an optimizer
+
+| Optimizer | Inner strength | Outer strength | Input-statistic momentum |
+|---|---:|---:|---|
+| `MuonT` / `FastMuonT` | ½ | ⅛ | Matches `momentum` by default |
+| `AdamT` / `FastAdamT` | ¼ | ¼ | Matches `betas[1]` by default |
+
+Both use shaped weight decay and take `lr` exactly as supplied. Set
+`statistic_momentum` explicitly when you want it to differ from the default.
+
+## Add Toner to your model
+
+Select the hidden `nn.Linear` layers to optimize. Embeddings, output heads,
+normalization gains, and biases belong in a separate optimizer; the
+[training example](examples/train_nanogpt.py) shows the complete setup.
+
+Set `matrix_lr` to the matrix learning rate for your training setup. To reproduce
+our experiments, use the value in the corresponding [reproduction config](#reproduce-a-comparison).
+
+```python
+from toner import ActivationStatistics, MuonT
+
+layers = {"projection": model.projection}
+optimizer = MuonT(
+    [layer.weight for layer in layers.values()],
+    lr=matrix_lr,
+    weight_decay=0.1,
+    momentum=0.95,
+    ns_mode="tpu",
+)
+statistics = ActivationStatistics(layers)
+
+optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
+with statistics.capture():
+    loss = compute_loss(model, batch)
+loss.backward()
+statistics.commit(optimizer)
+optimizer.step()
+
+statistics.close()  # once training is finished
+```
+
+For gradient accumulation, capture each forward and commit once per optimizer
+step. Capture only the forward pass so backward recomputation does not count
+inputs twice. With DDP, the collector pools input statistics across ranks;
+DDP synchronizes gradients separately.
+
+## Fast CUDA integration
+
+`FastMuonT` and `FastAdamT` compute statistics and factors alongside the final
+microbatch’s backward pass. Choose the adapter for your model:
+
+| Adapter | Projection layout |
+|---|---|
+| `NanoGPTBlock` | Modded-nanoGPT: separate Q/K/V, attention output, and a two-layer MLP |
+| `ProjectionBlock` | Llama-style: separate Q/K/V, attention output, and a gated MLP |
+
+The fast backend requires FP32 weights, BF16 activations, uniform block shapes,
+and hidden/MLP widths divisible by 256. The example selects it automatically
+on CUDA. See the [fast guide](docs/FAST.md) for integration and checkpointing.
+
+Use the general implementation for other `nn.Linear` layouts. It computes
+factors by eigendecomposition every step; MuonT still uses a finite
+Newton–Schulz iteration for its polar operation.
+
+---
+
+Apache-2.0 · [License](LICENSE)
+
+Mohamad Amin Mohamadi · Kaiyue Wen · Tianhao Wang · Zhiyuan Li

+# Fast CUDA path
+
+The fast backend computes sampled input Grams, pooled statistics and inverse-power factors on a
+side CUDA stream, overlapping the final microbatch's backward pass. It reuses a
+recent eigenbasis, refines factors from the current statistic every step, and
+repairs or falls back to exact eigendecomposition when needed. Refreshed host
+bases are installed when ready; optimizer updates use the current statistic,
+not a deliberately lagged root.
+
+## Usage
+
+Install the CUDA dependency with `pip install -e '.[fast]'`, then connect the
+optimizer to compatible projection blocks:
+
+```python
+from toner.fast import FastMuonT, NanoGPTBlock
+
+optimizer = FastMuonT(
+    [NanoGPTBlock.from_module(block) for block in model.blocks],
+    lr=matrix_lr,
+    weight_decay=0.1,
+    micro_batch_size=micro_batch_size,
+    sequence_length=sequence_length,
+    accumulation_steps=accumulation_steps,
+)
+
+optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
+for microbatch_index, batch in enumerate(microbatches):
+    with optimizer.capture_microbatch(), torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
+        loss = compute_loss(model, batch) / accumulation_steps
+    if microbatch_index == accumulation_steps - 1:
+        optimizer.begin()             # async statistics/roots before backward
+    loss.backward()
+optimizer.step()                     # waits for factors; gradients must already be synchronized
+# Step the separate auxiliary optimizer as well.
+# At the end, on every distributed rank:
+optimizer.close()
+```
+
+## Projection layouts
+
+`NanoGPTBlock.from_module(block)` maps the six hidden matrices in a modded-nanoGPT
+block: `attn.q`, `attn.k`, `attn.v`, `attn.proj`, `mlp.fc` and `mlp.proj`.
+Projection biases are allowed but remain in the auxiliary optimizer. Toner uses
+four input statistics: one shared by Q/K/V, plus one each for attention output,
+MLP expansion and MLP output.
+
+For uniform, bias-free Llama-style blocks, use
+`ProjectionBlock.from_module(block)` instead. This maps `q`, `k`, `v`, `o`,
+`gate`, `up` and `down`; gate/up share their input statistic.
+
+The fast and reference backends use different floating-point products and root
+computations, so their trajectories need not be bitwise identical.
+
+Choosing a layout does not change the optimizer's numerical rule. Both use the
+same FastMuonT or FastAdamT updates, current-step statistics and root engine.
+FastMuonT defaults to ten BF16-input/FP32-output Newton–Schulz iterations and raw
+momentum accumulation; `NanoGPTBlock` does not substitute a different Muon rule.
+
+## Supported integration
+
+- All blocks in one optimizer use the same layout and dimensions. Hidden and MLP
+  widths must be multiples of 256. Grouped-query attention, fused QKV and uneven
+  attention projection widths are not supported by these adapters.
+- Q/K/V share the same input tensor; Llama gate/up share another. Each configured
+  projection runs exactly once per captured microbatch, with the configured
+  batch and sequence shape. Capture ends before backward, excluding activation
+  recomputation.
+- Parameters are contiguous FP32 masters on one Ampere-or-newer CUDA GPU per
+  process. Inputs are BF16, or the forward runs under CUDA BF16 autocast. FP16
+  autocast is rejected. Capture, begin and step use the construction CUDA stream.
+  Sampled inputs must be finite and have nonzero second-moment trace; the retained
+  relative-ridge normalization is undefined for an all-zero input statistic.
+- Multi-GPU use requires an initialized default NCCL process group and replicated
+  parameters with synchronized gradients (e.g. DDP). The block count must divide
+  evenly across ranks. Statistics are pooled globally and updates are sharded
+  internally. FSDP/ZeRO-sharded parameters are not supported by this adapter.
+- Only one fast Toner optimizer may be active per process because the retained
+  root engine uses shared compiled configuration. Close it before creating another.
+- Fast MuonT supports the inverse-root strengths ⅛, ¼ and ½. Fast AdamT
+  retains matched quarters. Damping is fixed at 0.001. Use the
+  readable implementation for arbitrary strengths or damping.
+
+`lr` is the matrix learning rate and is used directly. FastMuonT inherits
+`statistic_momentum` from `momentum` when omitted or `None`; an explicit value
+overrides it. FastAdamT similarly inherits `betas[1]` when `statistic_momentum` is omitted or
+`None`.
+Update `optimizer.param_groups[0]["lr"]` to apply a learning-rate schedule;
+`weight_decay` in the same group is also read at every step. Embedding, output-head,
+normalization parameters and projection biases require a separate optimizer. The first twenty
+steps use exact roots by default. `root_inline_steps`, `root_iterations`,
+`root_refresh` and `root_graphs` expose the root-engine controls;
+changing them changes the numerical/performance configuration.
+
+## Checkpoints
+
+After a completed step, call `optimizer.state_dict()` on **every rank**. It is a
+collective operation; only rank zero receives the full CPU checkpoint. Save it
+along with model and auxiliary-optimizer state. To resume, broadcast/load the
+same optimizer checkpoint on every rank into a fresh optimizer with the same
+layout and settings. New checkpoints use `toner.fast.v3` and record the layout.
+The earlier `toner.fast.v2` format loads only into the Llama layout.
+
+Statistic EMAs and gradient moments are preserved. Root bases are recomputed and
+the exact-root startup phase restarts after loading, so resumed
+numerical trajectories need not be bitwise identical. The adapter validates the
+optimizer configuration and parameter names/shapes when loading. When finished,
+all ranks call `close()`: it waits for root work, detaches capture hooks and
+releases its own NCCL group without destroying the application’s default group.
+
+## Execution
+
+The adapter collects inputs with forward hooks. Call `begin()` after the last
+forward and before backward to overlap factor computation. Startup compilation
+and exact eigendecompositions can make the first steps slower.

+# Adapted from modded-nanoGPT: https://github.com/KellerJordan/modded-nanogpt

+# copies or substantial portions of the Software.
+#
+# THE SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, EXPRESS OR
+# IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY,
+# FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND NONINFRINGEMENT. IN NO EVENT SHALL THE
+# AUTHORS OR COPYRIGHT HOLDERS BE LIABLE FOR ANY CLAIM, DAMAGES OR OTHER
+# LIABILITY, WHETHER IN AN ACTION OF CONTRACT, TORT OR OTHERWISE, ARISING FROM,
+# OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THE SOFTWARE OR THE USE OR OTHER DEALINGS IN THE
+# SOFTWARE.
+
+"""A compact modded-nanoGPT model with separate attention projections."""
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import torch
+from torch import nn
+from torch.nn import functional as F
+
+
+@dataclass
+class GPTConfig:
+    vocab_size: int = 50304
+    n_layer: int = 12
+    n_embd: int = 768
+    head_dim: int = 128
+
+
+class RMSNorm(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, width):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.gains = nn.Parameter(torch.ones(width))
+
+    def forward(self, x):
+        return F.rms_norm(x, (x.size(-1),), weight=self.gains.to(x.dtype))
+
+
+class Linear(nn.Linear):
+    def __init__(self, in_features, out_features):
+        super().__init__(in_features, out_features, bias=True)
+
+    def forward(self, x):
+        return F.linear(x, self.weight.to(x.dtype), self.bias.to(x.dtype))
+
+
+class Rotary(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, head_dim):
+        super().__init__()
+        frequency = (1 / 1024) ** torch.linspace(0, 1, steps=head_dim // 4, dtype=torch.float32)
+        self.register_buffer("angular_freq", torch.cat([frequency, torch.zeros_like(frequency)]))
+
+    def forward(self, x):
+        position = torch.arange(x.size(1), device=x.device, dtype=torch.float32)
+        angle = torch.outer(position, self.angular_freq)[None, :, None, :]
+        left, right = x.float().chunk(2, dim=-1)
+        return torch.cat(
+            [left * angle.cos() + right * angle.sin(), -left * angle.sin() + right * angle.cos()],
+            dim=-1,
+        ).to(x.dtype)
+
+
+class CausalSelfAttention(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, width, head_dim):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.num_heads, self.head_dim = width // head_dim, head_dim
+        self.q, self.k, self.v = [Linear(width, width) for _ in range(3)]
+        self.proj = Linear(width, width)
+        self.rotary = Rotary(head_dim)
+
+    def forward(self, x):
+        batch, length, width = x.shape
+        q, k, v = [
+            layer(x).view(batch, length, self.num_heads, self.head_dim)
+            for layer in (self.q, self.k, self.v)
+        ]
+        q = self.rotary(F.rms_norm(q, (self.head_dim,)))
+        k = self.rotary(F.rms_norm(k, (self.head_dim,)))
+        output = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(
+            q.transpose(1, 2), k.transpose(1, 2), v.transpose(1, 2), scale=0.12, is_causal=True
+        )
+        return self.proj(output.transpose(1, 2).contiguous().view(batch, length, width))
+
+
+class MLP(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, width):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.fc, self.proj = Linear(width, 4 * width), Linear(4 * width, width)
+
+    def forward(self, x):
+        return self.proj(self.fc(x).relu().square())
+
+
+class Block(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, width, head_dim):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.norm1, self.norm2 = RMSNorm(width), RMSNorm(width)
+        self.attn, self.mlp = CausalSelfAttention(width, head_dim), MLP(width)
+
+    def forward(self, x):
+        x = x + self.attn(self.norm1(x))
+        return x + self.mlp(self.norm2(x))
+
+
+class GPT(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, config):
+        super().__init__()
+        if min(config.vocab_size, config.n_layer, config.n_embd, config.head_dim) < 1:
+            raise ValueError("Model dimensions must be positive")
+        if config.n_embd % config.head_dim or config.head_dim % 4:
+            raise ValueError("Width must divide into heads; head_dim must be divisible by four")
+        self.config = config
+        self.embed = nn.Embedding(config.vocab_size, config.n_embd)
+        self.blocks = nn.ModuleList(
+            [Block(config.n_embd, config.head_dim) for _ in range(config.n_layer)]
+        )
+        self.proj = Linear(config.n_embd, config.vocab_size)
+        self.norm1, self.norm2 = RMSNorm(config.n_embd), RMSNorm(config.n_embd)
+        with torch.no_grad():
+            for name, parameter in self.named_parameters():
+                if name.endswith("weight"):
+                    if "proj" in name:
+                        parameter.zero_()
+                    elif "embed" in name:
+                        parameter.normal_()
+                    else:
+                        parameter.normal_(std=(0.33 / parameter.size(-1)) ** 0.5)
+                elif name.endswith("bias"):
+                    parameter.zero_()
+                else:
+                    parameter.fill_(1)
+
+    def forward(self, tokens, targets=None):
+        x = self.embed(tokens)
+        if x.is_cuda:
+            x = x.bfloat16()
+        x = self.norm1(x)
+        for block in self.blocks:
+            x = block(x)
+        logits = self.proj(self.norm2(x)).float()
+        logits = 15 * logits * (logits.square() + 15**2).rsqrt()
+        loss = None if targets is None else F.cross_entropy(logits.flatten(0, 1), targets.flatten())
+        return logits, loss

+"""Prepare character-level train.bin / val.bin files from UTF-8 text."""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+from urllib.request import urlopen
+
+import numpy as np
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--input", type=Path, help="UTF-8 file; defaults to downloading Shakespeare"
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=Path("data/shakespeare_char"))
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    if args.input:
+        text = args.input.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+    else:
+        url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karpathy/char-rnn/master/data/tinyshakespeare/input.txt"
+        text = urlopen(url, timeout=60).read().decode("utf-8")
+    chars = sorted(set(text))
+    if not chars or len(chars) > 65536 or len(text) < 20:
+        parser.error("Expected nonempty text with at most 65,536 distinct characters")
+    encoding = {char: index for index, char in enumerate(chars)}
+    tokens = np.fromiter((encoding[char] for char in text), dtype=np.uint16, count=len(text))
+    cut = int(len(tokens) * 0.9)
+    args.out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    tokens[:cut].tofile(args.out / "train.bin")
+    tokens[cut:].tofile(args.out / "val.bin")
+    (args.out / "meta.json").write_text(
+        json.dumps({"vocab_size": len(chars), "characters": chars}, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"
+    )
+    print(
+        f"Prepared {cut:,} training and {len(tokens) - cut:,} validation tokens; vocabulary {len(chars)}"
+    )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+"""Train modded-nanoGPT with MuonT or AdamT on prepared train.bin / val.bin token files."""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import numpy as np
+import torch
+from torch import nn
+
+from toner import ActivationStatistics, MuonT, AdamT
+from model import GPT, GPTConfig
+
+
+def build_optimizers(model, args, backend):
+    """Partition hidden weights and construct their optimizers and input capture."""
+    layers = {
+        name: layer
+        for name, layer in model.named_modules()
+        if isinstance(layer, nn.Linear) and name.startswith("blocks.")
+    }
+    matrices = [layer.weight for layer in layers.values()]
+    matrix_ids = {id(p) for p in matrices}
+    auxiliary_parameters = [p for p in model.parameters() if id(p) not in matrix_ids]
+    options = dict(lr=args.lr, weight_decay=args.weight_decay)
+    if args.optimizer == "muon":
+        options.update(momentum=args.momentum, statistic_momentum=args.statistic_momentum)
+    else:
+        options["eps"] = 1e-15
+        if args.statistic_momentum is not None:
+            options["statistic_momentum"] = args.statistic_momentum
+    if backend == "fast":
+        from toner.fast import FastMuonT, FastAdamT, NanoGPTBlock
+
+        blocks = [NanoGPTBlock.from_module(block) for block in model.blocks]
+        optimizer_cls = FastMuonT if args.optimizer == "muon" else FastAdamT
+        optimizer = optimizer_cls(
+            blocks,
+            micro_batch_size=args.batch_size,
+            sequence_length=args.block_size,
+            accumulation_steps=args.accumulation_steps,
+            **options,
+        )
+        statistics = None
+    else:
+        if args.optimizer == "muon":
+            options["ns_mode"] = "tpu" if args.device == "cuda" else "f32"
+        optimizer_cls = MuonT if args.optimizer == "muon" else AdamT
+        optimizer = optimizer_cls(matrices, **options)
+        statistics = ActivationStatistics(layers)
+    # Embedding, untied output head, biases and norm gains use separate AdamW.
+    auxiliary = torch.optim.AdamW(auxiliary_parameters, lr=args.aux_lr, weight_decay=0.0)
+
+    return optimizer, auxiliary, statistics, auxiliary_parameters
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--data-dir", type=Path, default=Path("data/shakespeare_char"))
+    parser.add_argument("--vocab-size", type=int, help="Defaults to meta.json in data-dir")
+    parser.add_argument("--backend", choices=["auto", "reference", "fast"], default="auto")
+    parser.add_argument("--optimizer", choices=["muon", "adam"], default="muon")
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--device", choices=["cpu", "cuda"], default="cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--steps", type=int, default=1000)
+    parser.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=8)
+    parser.add_argument("--block-size", type=int, default=128)
+    parser.add_argument("--layers", type=int, default=4)
+    parser.add_argument("--head-dim", type=int, default=128)
+    parser.add_argument("--width", type=int, default=256)
+    parser.add_argument("--lr", type=float, default=0.002)
+    parser.add_argument("--aux-lr", type=float, default=0.0006)
+    parser.add_argument("--weight-decay", type=float, default=0.1)
+    parser.add_argument("--momentum", type=float, default=0.95)
+    parser.add_argument("--statistic-momentum", type=float, default=None)
+    parser.add_argument("--accumulation-steps", type=int, default=1)
+    parser.add_argument("--eval-every", type=int, default=100)
+    parser.add_argument("--eval-batches", type=int, default=10)
+    parser.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=Path("checkpoints/nanogpt.pt"))
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    for key in (
+        "steps",
+        "batch_size",
+        "block_size",
+        "layers",
+        "head_dim",
+        "width",
+        "accumulation_steps",
+        "eval_every",
+        "eval_batches",
+    ):
+        if getattr(args, key) < 1:
+            parser.error(f"{key} must be positive")
+    if args.width % args.head_dim or args.head_dim % 4:
+        parser.error("width must divide into heads, and head-dim must be divisible by four")
+    if args.vocab_size is None:
+        meta = args.data_dir / "meta.json"
+        if not meta.is_file():
+            parser.error("Supply --vocab-size or a data-dir containing meta.json")
+        args.vocab_size = json.loads(meta.read_text())["vocab_size"]
+    if not isinstance(args.vocab_size, int) or args.vocab_size < 1:
+        parser.error("vocab-size must be a positive integer")
+    backend = (
+        ("fast" if args.device == "cuda" else "reference")
+        if args.backend == "auto"
+        else args.backend
+    )
+    if backend == "fast" and (args.device != "cuda" or args.width % 256):
+        parser.error("fast backend needs CUDA and width divisible by 256")
+    data = {}
+    for split in ("train", "val"):
+        file = args.data_dir / f"{split}.bin"
+        if not file.is_file() or file.stat().st_size % 2:
+            parser.error(f"Expected a uint16 token file: {file}")
+        data[split] = np.memmap(file, dtype=np.uint16, mode="r")
+        if len(data[split]) <= args.block_size:
+            parser.error(f"{split}.bin is too short for block-size={args.block_size}")
+        if int(data[split].max()) >= args.vocab_size:
+            parser.error(f"{split}.bin contains token IDs outside --vocab-size")
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    train_rng, eval_rng = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0), torch.Generator().manual_seed(1)
+
+    def batch(split):
+        tokens = data[split]
+        starts = torch.randint(
+            len(tokens) - args.block_size,
+            (args.batch_size,),
+            generator=train_rng if split == "train" else eval_rng,
+        )
+        x = torch.stack(
+            [
+                torch.from_numpy(np.array(tokens[i : i + args.block_size], dtype=np.int64))
+                for i in starts.tolist()
+            ]
+        )
+        y = torch.stack(
+            [
+                torch.from_numpy(np.array(tokens[i + 1 : i + args.block_size + 1], dtype=np.int64))
+                for i in starts.tolist()
+            ]
+        )
+        return x.to(args.device), y.to(args.device)
+
+    config = GPTConfig(
+        vocab_size=args.vocab_size, n_layer=args.layers, n_embd=args.width, head_dim=args.head_dim
+    )
+    model = GPT(config).to(args.device)
+    optimizer, auxiliary, statistics, auxiliary_parameters = build_optimizers(model, args, backend)
+
+    def autocast():
+        return torch.autocast(args.device, dtype=torch.bfloat16, enabled=args.device == "cuda")
+
+    @torch.no_grad()
+    def evaluate():
+        model.eval()
+        losses = []
+        for _ in range(args.eval_batches):
+            with autocast():
+                _, loss = model(*batch("val"))
+            losses.append(loss.item())
+        model.train()
+        return sum(losses) / len(losses)
+
+    try:
+        model.train()
+        for step in range(1, args.steps + 1):
+            optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
+            auxiliary.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
+            loss_sum = 0.0
+            for micro in range(args.accumulation_steps):
+                capture = (
+                    optimizer.capture_microbatch() if backend == "fast" else statistics.capture()
+                )
+                with capture, autocast():
+                    _, loss = model(*batch("train"))
+                if backend == "fast" and micro == args.accumulation_steps - 1:
+                    optimizer.begin()  # overlap current-step statistics and factors with backward
+                (loss / args.accumulation_steps).backward()
+                loss_sum += loss.item() / args.accumulation_steps
+            torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(
+                auxiliary_parameters if args.optimizer == "muon" else model.parameters(), 1.0
+            )
+            if statistics is not None:
+                statistics.commit(optimizer)
+            optimizer.step()
+            auxiliary.step()
+            if step == 1 or step % args.eval_every == 0 or step == args.steps:
+                print(f"step {step}: train {loss_sum:.4f}, val {evaluate():.4f}", flush=True)
+        args.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        torch.save(
+            {
+                "model": model.state_dict(),
+                "model_config": vars(config),
+                "step": args.steps,
+                "backend": backend,
+                "optimizer": optimizer.state_dict(),
+                "auxiliary_optimizer": auxiliary.state_dict(),
+            },
+            args.out,
+        )
+    finally:
+        if statistics is not None:
+            statistics.close()
+        else:
+            optimizer.close()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+# Reproduce the Marin comparisons
+
+This directory contains the **1× training-budget runs in Figure 1**: Muon,
+MuonT with strengths (½, ⅛) and (¼, ¼), and the plotted AdamW/AdamT comparisons.
+Each JSON config specifies the model, batch, schedule, optimizer settings and
+reference final C4 validation loss.
+
+| Model | Training tokens | Muon / MuonT batches | AdamW / AdamT batches | Configs |
+|---|---:|---|---|---|
+| 130M | 2.68B | 0.5M, 1M, 2M, 4M | 1M, 2M, 4M | [130M](configs/130m) |
+| 300M | 6.04B | 0.5M, 1M, 2M, 4M | 1M, 2M, 4M | [300M](configs/300m) |
+| 520M | 10.74B | 0.5M, 1M, 2M, 4M | 2M, 4M | [520M](configs/520m) |
+| 1.2B | 24.16B | 1M, 2M, 4M, 8M | — | [1.2B](configs/1p2b) |
+
+Batch labels use powers of two: 1M means 1,048,576 tokens. Exact budgets are
+in each config; rounding to complete updates can slightly change the budget.
+Files named `muont_*.json` use (½, ⅛); `muont_quarter_*.json` use (¼, ¼).
+
+## Prepare the data
+
+Install the data tools and accept the relevant dataset/tokenizer access terms
+on Hugging Face, then authenticate with `hf auth login`:
+
+```bash
+pip install -e '.[examples,fast,marin-data]'
+python reproduce/marin/prepare_data.py --out data/marin --workers 8
+```
+
+The preparation script uses fixed revisions of DCLM, StarCoderData and
+Proof-Pile-2, tokenized with Llama 3.1's tokenizer. It also prepares all 16
+Paloma validation subsets, including C4. The training token files occupy
+approximately **102 GB**, excluding download caches and validation data.
+
+[`data_plan.json`](data_plan.json) fixes source files, document-prefix quotas,
+output order and expected token/document counts. Preparation checks those
+counts before accepting a shard and stores a checksum for subsequent checks.
+Use `--check-only` to check an existing directory. These generated checksums
+protect file integrity; the original token files did not have recorded hashes.
+For existing files without checksum receipts, document-count checks assume each
+EOS marks one document. The tokenizer revision is pinned to the
+available cached snapshot. Use `--split train` or `--split validation` to prepare
+these separately.
+
+For background on Marin's data and training pipeline, see the
+[Marin documentation](https://marin.readthedocs.io/en/latest/). Use the fixed
+plan here for these PyTorch runs rather than today's default data mixture.
+
+## Train
+
+The PyTorch configurations use eight CUDA GPUs, BF16 computation, a 4,096-token
+context and document-packed attention. The recorded attention backend is FA3
+on H100 GPUs. Install a PyTorch build that provides FA3 and the matching CUDA
+and Triton dependencies. The integration checks use PyTorch 2.11 and Triton 3.6;
+FA3 requires a compatible Hopper setup.
+
+```bash
+torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=8 --module reproduce.marin.train \
+    --config reproduce/marin/configs/130m/muon_1m.json \
+    --data data/marin --out runs/marin_130m_muon_1m
+
+torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=8 --module reproduce.marin.train \
+    --config reproduce/marin/configs/130m/muont_1m.json \
+    --data data/marin --out runs/marin_130m_muont_1m
+```
+
+Choose another config to change the model, optimizer or batch. Learning rates
+are explicit: no transfer multiplier is applied by the runner. The configs also
+preserve input-statistic momentum, fast-root settings, matrix chunking and the
+older 300M Muon baseline's distinct embedding initialization.
+
+Toner collects sampled layer inputs during the forward pass and overlaps
+statistic/factor computation with backpropagation. This runner uses the
+recomputation-based capture from the Marin experiments, rather than the general
+package's forward-hook adapter.
+
+The runner evaluates C4, the metric in Figure 1, rather than every Paloma subset.
+Add `--max-steps 2` for an early-stop execution check with the configured batch
+and schedule. The final model and loss log are saved under `--out`; this is not
+a training-resume interface.
+
+The reported losses are reference outcomes. Software, hardware and numerical
+execution can affect reproduced losses; matching a configuration does not
+promise bitwise-identical training.
+
+## Native Marin baselines
+
+The Muon references at 520M/0.5M and 1.2B/1M come from Marin's native JAX runs. Their configs retain the recorded model, optimizer, data mixture, and training settings. They do not run through the PyTorch trainer.
+
+To export these settings for inspection:
+
+```bash
+python reproduce/marin/native.py reproduce/marin/configs/520m/muon_0p5m.json --output /tmp/muon-520m-native.json
+```
+
+The original runtime is not fully recovered. The 520M run records Levanter `1.2.dev1190`, Haliax `1.4.dev327`, and JAX/JAXlib `0.5.0`, but that published Levanter wheel does not contain Muon. The 1.2B run's resumed-run metadata lists multiple Levanter, Haliax, and JAX versions. We therefore provide recorded settings rather than an unverified installation or launch command. The recorded Git commits identify **Marin**, not Levanter. Native data settings use Marin's original tokenized caches, not the PyTorch data plan.

+"""Deterministic uint32 token streams and the Marin training mixture."""
+
+import os
+import resource
+
+import numpy as np
+
+# every shard stays memory-mapped (one descriptor each; the image has ~2,300 shards): raise the soft limit to the hard one
+_soft, _hard = resource.getrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_NOFILE)
+if _soft != resource.RLIM_INFINITY and (_hard == resource.RLIM_INFINITY or _soft < _hard):
+    resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_NOFILE, (_hard, _hard))
+
+SEQ = 4096
+WEIGHTS = {
+    "dclm": 3.8,
+    "starcoder": 0.25,
+    "proofpile": 0.055,
+}  # Marin's DCLM mixture (unnormalized)
+
+
+class Stream:
+    """A component's token stream: its shards back to back, read as windows of `seq` tokens."""
+
+    def __init__(self, files, seq=SEQ):
+        files = [
+            f for f in files if os.path.getsize(f) > 0
+        ]  # a source file can be empty (e.g. 5 tiny ProofPile files)
+        self.mm = [np.memmap(f, dtype=np.uint32, mode="r") for f in files]
+        self.sizes = np.array([m.size for m in self.mm], dtype=np.int64)
+        self.cum = np.concatenate(([0], np.cumsum(self.sizes)))
+        self.seq = seq
+        self.n_windows = int(self.cum[-1] // seq)
+
+    def window(self, w):
+        start, end = w * self.seq, (w + 1) * self.seq
+        s = int(np.searchsorted(self.cum, start, side="right") - 1)
+        parts, pos = [], start
+        while pos < end:
+            off = pos - self.cum[s]
+            take = min(end - pos, self.sizes[s] - off)
+            parts.append(self.mm[s][off : off + take])
+            pos += take
+            s += 1
+        return parts[0] if len(parts) == 1 else np.concatenate(parts)
+
+
+class MarinMixture:
+    def __init__(self, root, weights=WEIGHTS, seq=SEQ, block_size=2048, seed=0, heldout_windows=0):
+        self.block_size, self.seed = block_size, seed
+        self.names = list(weights)
+        self.streams, self.perms, self.heldout = [], [], []
+        for i, name in enumerate(self.names):
+            files = sorted(
+                os.path.join(root, name, f)
+                for f in os.listdir(os.path.join(root, name))
+                if f.endswith(".bin")
+            )
+            st = Stream(files, seq)
+            # `heldout_windows` random windows of each stream are never trained on (a held-out set from the same data)
+            perm = np.random.default_rng([seed, i]).permutation(st.n_windows)
+            self.streams.append(st)
+            self.perms.append(perm[heldout_windows:])
+            self.heldout.append(np.sort(perm[:heldout_windows]))
+        wsum = sum(weights.values())
+        counts = np.zeros(len(self.names), dtype=np.int32)
+        for i, name in enumerate(self.names):
+            counts[i] = (
+                weights[name] / wsum * block_size
+            )  # truncation, as Levanter's int32 assignment
+        counts[np.argmax(counts)] += block_size - counts.sum()
+        self.counts = counts
+        self.base = np.concatenate(
+            [np.stack((np.full(c, i), np.arange(c)), 1) for i, c in enumerate(counts)]
+        )
+        self._block = (None, None)
+
+    def describe(self):
+        return {
+            n: {
+                "windows": st.n_windows,
+                "tokens": int(st.cum[-1]),
+                "per_block": int(c),
+                "epochs_per_1B_train_tokens": 1e9 * c / self.block_size / (st.n_windows * st.seq),
+            }
+            for n, st, c in zip(self.names, self.streams, self.counts)
+        }
+
+    def _block_ids(self, b):
+        if self._block[0] != b:
+            perm = np.random.default_rng([self.seed, 1 << 20, b]).permutation(self.block_size)
+            self._block = (b, self.base[perm])
+        return self._block[1]
+
+    def source(self, g):
+        """(component, window) of global sequence g."""
+        b, j = divmod(g, self.block_size)
+        comp, k = self._block_ids(b)[j]
+        idx = b * int(self.counts[comp]) + int(k)
+        perm = self.perms[comp]
+        return int(comp), int(perm[idx % perm.size])
+
+    def sequence(self, g):
+        comp, w = self.source(g)
+        return self.streams[comp].window(w)
+
+    def batch(self, start, n):
+        return np.stack([self.sequence(g) for g in range(start, start + n)])
+
+
+class EvalSet:
+    """An evaluation set: a token stream cut into seq windows (the last partial window dropped), as Levanter's eval."""
+
+    def __init__(self, files, seq=SEQ, windows=None):
+        self.stream = Stream(files, seq)
+        self.windows = np.arange(self.stream.n_windows) if windows is None else np.asarray(windows)
+
+    def __len__(self):
+        return len(self.windows)
+
+    def batch(self, start, n):
+        return np.stack([self.stream.window(int(w)) for w in self.windows[start : start + n]])
+
+
+def eval_sets(root, mixture=None, include=None, seq=SEQ):
+    """Paloma subsets found under root/paloma (each <subset>/*.bin) plus the held-out mixture windows."""
+    out = {}
+    pal = os.path.join(root, "paloma")
+    if os.path.isdir(pal):
+        for sub in sorted(os.listdir(pal)):
+            files = sorted(
+                os.path.join(pal, sub, f)
+                for f in os.listdir(os.path.join(pal, sub))
+                if f.endswith(".bin")
+            )
+            if files and (include is None or sub in include):
+                es = EvalSet(files, seq=seq)
+                if len(es):
+                    out[f"paloma/{sub}"] = es
+    if mixture is not None:
+        for name, st, held in zip(mixture.names, mixture.streams, mixture.heldout):
+            if held.size:
+                es = EvalSet.__new__(EvalSet)
+                es.stream, es.windows = st, held
+                out[f"heldout/{name}"] = es
+    return out
+
+
+def pack(tokens, CAP, EOS=128001, pin_memory=True):
+    """Pack EOS-separated attention; only each window's final target is masked."""
+    import torch
+
+    B, T = tokens.shape
+    tok = tokens.astype(np.int64)
+    tgt = np.empty_like(tok)
+    tgt[:, :-1], tgt[:, -1] = tok[:, 1:], -100
+    starts = np.zeros((B, T), dtype=bool)
+    starts[:, 0] = True
+    starts[:, 1:] = tok[:, :-1] == EOS
+    idx = np.flatnonzero(starts.reshape(-1)).astype(np.int32)
+    n = idx.size
+    if n >= CAP:
+        raise ValueError(f"{n} documents exceed attention capacity {CAP}")
+    cu = np.full(CAP + 1, B * T, dtype=np.int32)
+    cu[:n] = idx
+    mx = int(np.diff(np.append(idx, B * T)).max())
+    values = [torch.from_numpy(a) for a in (tok, tgt, cu)]
+    if pin_memory:
+        values = [a.pin_memory() for a in values]
+    return (*values, torch.tensor([n, mx], dtype=torch.int64))
+
+
+def validate_data_plan(root, plan_path):
+    """Check shard names and token counts before constructing the deterministic mixture."""
+    import json
+    from pathlib import Path
+
+    root = Path(root)
+    with open(plan_path) as stream:
+        plan = json.load(stream)
+    required = set(WEIGHTS) | {"paloma/c4_en"}
+    for component in required:
+        records = [r for r in plan["files"] if r["component"] == component]
+        if not records:
+            raise ValueError(f"No data records for {component}")
+        expected = {r["file"] for r in records}
+        directory = root / component
+        actual = {p.name for p in directory.glob("*.bin")}
+        if actual != expected:
+            raise ValueError(f"Shard names differ from data plan for {component}")
+        for record in records:
+            path = directory / record["file"]
+            if path.stat().st_size != 4 * record["tokens"]:
+                raise ValueError(f"Token count differs from data plan: {path}")

+"""BF16 language-model head and token cross entropy."""
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+IGNORE = -100
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _fwd_kernel(
+    h_ptr,
+    w_ptr,
+    z_ptr,
+    pmax_ptr,
+    psum_ptr,
+    M,
+    N,
+    K,
+    shm,
+    shk,
+    swn,
+    swk,
+    szm,
+    szn,
+    NT,
+    BM: tl.constexpr,
+    BN: tl.constexpr,
+    BK: tl.constexpr,
+    GROUP: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    pid = tl.program_id(0)
+    npm, npn = tl.cdiv(M, BM), tl.cdiv(N, BN)
+    gid = pid // (GROUP * npn)
+    first = gid * GROUP
+    gs = min(npm - first, GROUP)
+    pm = first + (pid % gs)
+    pn = (pid % (GROUP * npn)) // gs
+    rm = pm * BM + tl.arange(0, BM)
+    rn = pn * BN + tl.arange(0, BN)
+    rk = tl.arange(0, BK)
+    acc = tl.zeros((BM, BN), tl.float32)
+    for k0 in range(0, K, BK):
+        a = tl.load(
+            h_ptr + rm[:, None] * shm + (k0 + rk)[None, :] * shk, mask=rm[:, None] < M, other=0.0
+        )
+        b = tl.load(
+            w_ptr + rn[None, :] * swn + (k0 + rk)[:, None] * swk, mask=rn[None, :] < N, other=0.0
+        )
+        acc = tl.dot(a, b, acc)
+    zb = acc.to(tl.bfloat16)
+    msk = (rm[:, None] < M) & (rn[None, :] < N)
+    # 64-bit row base: M x N exceeds 2^31 from M = 16,744 rows at the Llama-3 vocabulary (int32 offsets wrap around)
+    z_rows = z_ptr + (pm * BM).to(tl.int64) * szm
+    tl.store(z_rows + tl.arange(0, BM)[:, None] * szm + rn[None, :] * szn, zb, mask=msk)
+    zf = tl.where(rn[None, :] < N, zb.to(tl.float32), float("-inf"))
+    mx = tl.max(zf, 1)
+    s = tl.sum(tl.exp(zf - mx[:, None]), 1)
+    tl.store(pmax_ptr + rm * NT + pn, mx, mask=rm < M)
+    tl.store(psum_ptr + rm * NT + pn, s, mask=rm < M)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _lse_kernel(pmax_ptr, psum_ptr, z_ptr, t_ptr, lse_ptr, loss_ptr, NT, szm, BT: tl.constexpr):
+    row = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+    m = tl.full([BT], float("-inf"), tl.float32)
+    s = tl.zeros([BT], tl.float32)
+    for j0 in range(0, NT, BT):
+        j = j0 + tl.arange(0, BT)
+        pm = tl.load(pmax_ptr + row * NT + j, mask=j < NT, other=float("-inf"))
+        ps = tl.load(psum_ptr + row * NT + j, mask=j < NT, other=0.0)
+        mn = tl.maximum(m, pm)
+        s = s * tl.exp(tl.where(mn == float("-inf"), 0.0, m - mn)) + ps * tl.exp(
+            tl.where(mn == float("-inf"), 0.0, pm - mn)
+        )
+        m = mn
+    mx = tl.max(m, 0)
+    lse = mx + tl.log(tl.sum(s * tl.exp(m - mx), 0))
+    t = tl.load(t_ptr + row)
+    valid = t != -100
+    zt = tl.load(z_ptr + row * szm + tl.where(valid, t, 0)).to(tl.float32)
+    tl.store(lse_ptr + row, lse)
+    tl.store(loss_ptr + row, tl.where(valid, lse - zt, 0.0))
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _dz_tile(z_ptr, lse_ptr, t_ptr, g_ptr, r0, rn, M, N, szm, szn, BR: tl.constexpr):
+    # dz for rows r0 ... r0 + BR - 1 and columns rn, rounded to bf16 (reference rounding point); 0 outside the matrix.
+    # The row base is 64-bit (M x N can exceed 2^31); offsets within the tile stay 32-bit.
+    rl = tl.arange(0, BR)
+    rm = r0 + rl
+    msk = (rm[:, None] < M) & (rn[None, :] < N)
+    z = tl.load(
+        z_ptr + r0.to(tl.int64) * szm + rl[:, None] * szm + rn[None, :] * szn, mask=msk, other=0.0
+    ).to(tl.float32)
+    lse = tl.load(lse_ptr + rm, mask=rm < M, other=0.0)
+    t = tl.load(t_ptr + rm, mask=rm < M, other=-100)
+    g = tl.load(g_ptr + rm, mask=rm < M, other=0.0)
+    g = tl.where(t != -100, g, 0.0)
+    d = (tl.exp(z - lse[:, None]) - tl.where(rn[None, :] == t[:, None], 1.0, 0.0)) * g[:, None]
+    return tl.where(msk, d, 0.0).to(tl.bfloat16)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _dh_kernel(
+    z_ptr,
+    lse_ptr,
+    t_ptr,
+    g_ptr,
+    w_ptr,
+    dh_ptr,
+    M,
+    N,
+    K,
+    szm,
+    szn,
+    swn,
+    swk,
+    sdm,
+    sdk,
+    BM: tl.constexpr,
+    BK_OUT: tl.constexpr,
+    BN_RED: tl.constexpr,
+    GROUP: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    # dh[M, K] = dz[M, N] @ W[N, K]; the reduction runs over the vocabulary N
+    pid = tl.program_id(0)
+    npm, npk = tl.cdiv(M, BM), tl.cdiv(K, BK_OUT)
+    gid = pid // (GROUP * npk)
+    first = gid * GROUP
+    gs = min(npm - first, GROUP)
+    pm = first + (pid % gs)
+    pk = (pid % (GROUP * npk)) // gs
+    rm = pm * BM + tl.arange(0, BM)
+    rko = pk * BK_OUT + tl.arange(0, BK_OUT)
+    acc = tl.zeros((BM, BK_OUT), tl.float32)
+    for n0 in range(0, N, BN_RED):
+        rn = n0 + tl.arange(0, BN_RED)
+        dz = _dz_tile(z_ptr, lse_ptr, t_ptr, g_ptr, pm * BM, rn, M, N, szm, szn, BM)
+        w = tl.load(w_ptr + rn[:, None] * swn + rko[None, :] * swk, mask=rn[:, None] < N, other=0.0)
+        acc = tl.dot(dz, w, acc)
+    tl.store(
+        dh_ptr + rm[:, None] * sdm + rko[None, :] * sdk, acc.to(tl.bfloat16), mask=rm[:, None] < M
+    )
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _dw_kernel(
+    z_ptr,
+    lse_ptr,
+    t_ptr,
+    g_ptr,
+    h_ptr,
+    dw_ptr,
+    M,
+    N,
+    K,
+    szm,
+    szn,
+    shm,
+    shk,
+    sdn,
+    sdk,
+    BN: tl.constexpr,
+    BK_OUT: tl.constexpr,
+    BM_RED: tl.constexpr,
+    GROUP: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    # dW[N, K] = dz[M, N]^T @ h[M, K]; the reduction runs over tokens M
+    pid = tl.program_id(0)
+    npn, npk = tl.cdiv(N, BN), tl.cdiv(K, BK_OUT)
+    gid = pid // (GROUP * npk)
+    first = gid * GROUP
+    gs = min(npn - first, GROUP)
+    pn = first + (pid % gs)
+    pk = (pid % (GROUP * npk)) // gs
+    rn = pn * BN + tl.arange(0, BN)
+    rko = pk * BK_OUT + tl.arange(0, BK_OUT)
+    acc = tl.zeros((BN, BK_OUT), tl.float32)
+    for m0 in range(0, M, BM_RED):
+        rm = m0 + tl.arange(0, BM_RED)
+        dz = _dz_tile(z_ptr, lse_ptr, t_ptr, g_ptr, m0, rn, M, N, szm, szn, BM_RED)  # [BM_RED, BN]
+        h = tl.load(h_ptr + rm[:, None] * shm + rko[None, :] * shk, mask=rm[:, None] < M, other=0.0)
+        acc = tl.dot(tl.trans(dz), h, acc)
+    # autocast reference: the bf16 weight copy gets a bf16 gradient, then the cast back to the f32 master
+    tl.store(
+        dw_ptr + rn[:, None] * sdn + rko[None, :] * sdk,
+        acc.to(tl.bfloat16).to(tl.float32),
+        mask=rn[:, None] < N,
+    )
+
+
+CFG = {"fwd": (256, 128, 64, 8, 2), "dh": (128, 256, 64, 8, 2), "dw": (128, 256, 64, 8, 2)}
+
+
+def head_ce_forward(h, w_bf16, t):
+    M, K = h.shape
+    N = w_bf16.shape[0]
+    BM, BN, BK, nw, ns = CFG["fwd"]
+    NT = triton.cdiv(N, BN)
+    z = torch.empty(M, N, device=h.device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    pmax = torch.empty(M, NT, device=h.device, dtype=torch.float32)
+    psum = torch.empty(M, NT, device=h.device, dtype=torch.float32)
+    _fwd_kernel[(triton.cdiv(M, BM) * NT,)](
+        h,
+        w_bf16,
+        z,
+        pmax,
+        psum,
+        M,
+        N,
+        K,
+        h.stride(0),
+        h.stride(1),
+        w_bf16.stride(0),
+        w_bf16.stride(1),
+        z.stride(0),
+        z.stride(1),
+        NT,
+        BM=BM,
+        BN=BN,
+        BK=BK,
+        GROUP=8,
+        num_warps=nw,
+        num_stages=ns,
+    )
+    lse = torch.empty(M, device=h.device, dtype=torch.float32)
+    loss = torch.empty(M, device=h.device, dtype=torch.float32)
+    _lse_kernel[(M,)](pmax, psum, z, t, lse, loss, NT, z.stride(0), BT=512, num_warps=4)
+    return z, lse, loss
+
+
+def head_ce_backward(z, lse, t, grow, h, w_bf16):
+    M, N = z.shape
+    K = h.shape[1]
+    BM, BKo, BNr, nw, ns = CFG["dh"]
+    dh = torch.empty(M, K, device=h.device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    _dh_kernel[(triton.cdiv(M, BM) * triton.cdiv(K, BKo),)](
+        z,
+        lse,
+        t,
+        grow,
+        w_bf16,
+        dh,
+        M,
+        N,
+        K,
+        z.stride(0),
+        z.stride(1),
+        w_bf16.stride(0),
+        w_bf16.stride(1),
+        dh.stride(0),
+        dh.stride(1),
+        BM=BM,
+        BK_OUT=BKo,
+        BN_RED=BNr,
+        GROUP=8,
+        num_warps=nw,
+        num_stages=ns,
+    )
+    BN, BKo2, BMr, nw2, ns2 = CFG["dw"]
+    dw = torch.empty(N, K, device=h.device, dtype=torch.float32)
+    _dw_kernel[(triton.cdiv(N, BN) * triton.cdiv(K, BKo2),)](
+        z,
+        lse,
+        t,
+        grow,
+        h,
+        dw,
+        M,
+        N,
+        K,
+        z.stride(0),
+        z.stride(1),
+        h.stride(0),
+        h.stride(1),
+        dw.stride(0),
+        dw.stride(1),
+        BN=BN,
+        BK_OUT=BKo2,
+        BM_RED=BMr,
+        GROUP=8,
+        num_warps=nw2,
+        num_stages=ns2,
+    )
+    return dh, dw
+
+
+class HeadCE(torch.autograd.Function):
+    """loss = mean over valid rows of CE(bf16(h @ W^T), t); h bf16 [M,K], W f32 master [N,K] (cast to bf16 inside)."""
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def forward(ctx, h, W, t):

+        nvalid = (t != IGNORE).sum()
+        ctx.save_for_backward(z, lse, t, h, wb, nvalid)
+        return loss_rows.sum() / nvalid
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def backward(ctx, gout):
+        z, lse, t, h, wb, nvalid = ctx.saved_tensors
+        grow = (gout / nvalid).float().expand(z.shape[0]).contiguous()
+        dh, dw = head_ce_backward(z, lse, t, grow, h, wb)
+        return dh, dw, None

+"""Marin Llama-style transformer with document-packed attention."""
+
+import math
+
+import torch
+from torch import nn
+from torch.nn import functional as F
+
+
+def norm(layer, x, residual_dtype="bf16"):
+    if residual_dtype == "f32":
+        return layer(x)
+    xf = x.float()
+    out = (xf * torch.rsqrt(xf.square().mean(-1, keepdim=True) + layer.eps)).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    return layer.weight.to(torch.bfloat16) * out
+
+
+def sample_positions(sequence_length, head, stride):
+    return list(range(head)) + list(range(head + 1, sequence_length, stride))
+
+
+class Block(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, config, *, positions=None, row_capacity=0):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.config = config
+        h, m = config["hidden"], config["mlp"]
+        self.ln1, self.ln2 = (nn.RMSNorm(h, eps=config["norm_eps"]) for _ in range(2))
+        self.q, self.k, self.v, self.o = (nn.Linear(h, h, bias=False) for _ in range(4))
+        self.gate, self.up = (nn.Linear(h, m, bias=False) for _ in range(2))
+        self.down = nn.Linear(m, h, bias=False)
+        if positions is not None:
+            for kind, dim in (("attn", h), ("o", h), ("mlp", h), ("down", m)):
+                self.register_buffer(
+                    f"input_rows_{kind}",
+                    torch.zeros(row_capacity, dim, dtype=torch.bfloat16),
+                    persistent=False,
+                )
+            self.register_buffer("stat_idx", torch.tensor(positions), persistent=False)
+
+    def forward(self, x, cos, sin, cu, meta, captures=None):
+        from . import ops
+
+        c = self.config
+        B, T, H = x.shape
+        heads, hd = c["heads"], H // c["heads"]
+        x_in = x
+        h = norm(self.ln1, x, c["residual_dtype"])
+        q, k, v = (f(h).view(B, T, heads, hd) for f in (self.q, self.k, self.v))
+
+        def rotate(t):
+            return t * cos + torch.cat((-t[..., hd // 2 :], t[..., : hd // 2]), -1) * sin
+
+        q, k, v = rotate(q).to(torch.bfloat16), rotate(k).to(torch.bfloat16), v.to(torch.bfloat16)
+        a, _ = ops.doc_attn(
+            q.reshape(B * T, heads, hd),
+            k.reshape(B * T, heads, hd),
+            v.reshape(B * T, heads, hd),
+            cu,
+            meta,
+        )
+        a = a.view(B, T, H)
+        x = x + self.o(a)
+        h2 = norm(self.ln2, x, c["residual_dtype"])
+        g, u = self.gate(h2), self.up(h2)
+        m = F.silu(g) * u
+        if captures is not None:
+            captures.append(tuple(t.detach() for t in (x_in, a, x, g, u)))
+        return x + self.down(m)
+
+
+class Body(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, config, *, positions=None, row_capacity=0, rows_per_microbatch=0):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.config = config
+        h, hd = config["hidden"], config["hidden"] // config["heads"]
+        self.emb = nn.Embedding(config["vocab_size"], h)
+        self.blocks = nn.ModuleList(
+            Block(config, positions=positions, row_capacity=row_capacity)
+            for _ in range(config["layers"])
+        )
+        self.norm = nn.RMSNorm(h, eps=config["norm_eps"])
+        inv = 1.0 / config["rope_theta"] ** (torch.arange(0, hd, 2, dtype=torch.float32) / hd)
+        ang = torch.outer(torch.arange(config["sequence_length"], dtype=torch.float32), inv)
+        self.register_buffer("cos", torch.cat((ang, ang), -1).cos()[:, None], persistent=False)
+        self.register_buffer("sin", torch.cat((ang, ang), -1).sin()[:, None], persistent=False)
+        self.capture = positions is not None
+        if self.capture:
+            self.register_buffer("stat_at", torch.arange(rows_per_microbatch), persistent=False)
+
+    def forward(self, tokens, cu, meta):
+        x = self.emb(tokens)
+        if self.config["residual_dtype"] == "bf16":
+            x = x.to(torch.bfloat16)
+        captures = [] if self.capture else None
+        for block in self.blocks:
+            x = block(x, self.cos, self.sin, cu, meta, captures)
+        if self.capture:
+            from . import ops
+
+            xi, attn, xm, g, u = (list(c) for c in zip(*captures))
+            bufs = [
+                getattr(b, f"input_rows_{k}")
+                for b in self.blocks
+                for k in ("attn", "o", "mlp", "down")
+            ]
+            ops.capture_recomputed(
+                xi,
+                attn,
+                xm,
+                g,
+                u,
+                [b.ln1.weight.detach() for b in self.blocks],
+                [b.ln2.weight.detach() for b in self.blocks],
+                bufs,
+                self.stat_at,
+                self.blocks[0].stat_idx,
+                self.config["norm_eps"],
+            )
+        return norm(self.norm, x, self.config["residual_dtype"])
+
+
+class Model(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, config, **capture):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.body = Body(config, **capture)
+        self.head = nn.Linear(config["hidden"], config["vocab_size"], bias=False)
+
+
+def initialize_model(model, seed, embedding_scale="sqrt_hidden"):
+    """Truncated-normal initialization; the head is equal to the standard-scale embedding draw."""
+    if embedding_scale not in ("sqrt_hidden", "hidden"):
+        raise ValueError(f"Unknown embedding scale {embedding_scale}")
+    gen = torch.Generator(device=model.head.weight.device).manual_seed(seed)
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        for module in model.modules():
+            if isinstance(module, nn.Linear) and module is not model.head:
+                nn.init.trunc_normal_(module.weight, 0.0, 1.0, -3.0, 3.0, generator=gen).div_(
+                    math.sqrt(module.in_features)
+                )
+            elif isinstance(module, nn.RMSNorm):
+                nn.init.ones_(module.weight)
+        emb = model.body.emb.weight
+        nn.init.trunc_normal_(emb, 0.0, 1.0, -3.0, 3.0, generator=gen)
+        h = emb.shape[1]
+        model.head.weight.copy_(emb).div_(math.sqrt(h))
+        emb.div_(h if embedding_scale == "hidden" else math.sqrt(h))

+"""Export recorded native-JAX settings for the two published Muon references.
+
+This exports an inspection record, not a launch configuration: the original
+Muon-enabled Levanter source is not identified by the recorded package version.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def export_settings(config: dict) -> dict:
+    if config.get("engine") != "native_jax":
+        raise ValueError("Choose one of the two native_jax reference configs.")
+    return {
+        "status": "recorded settings; original Muon-enabled runtime required",
+        "reference_validation_loss": config["reference_validation_loss"],
+        **config["native"],
+    }
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("config", type=Path)
+    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True, type=Path)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    settings = export_settings(json.loads(args.config.read_text()))
+    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    args.output.write_text(json.dumps(settings, indent=2) + "\n")
+    print(f"Exported recorded settings to {args.output}; this is not a launch config.")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+# Ops shared by train.py and its tests.
+#   doc_attn: document-masked causal attention on a packed micro-batch (B*T tokens) with FlashAttention's varlen kernels
+#             (FA2, or FA3 once torch.nn.attention.activate_flash_attention_impl("FA3") is called on an H100).
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+
+# Capture sampled inputs through one opaque operation after the forward pass.
+@triton.jit
+def _gather_rows(tab, n, at, idx, P, D, s_b, s_t, BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
+    i = tl.program_id(0)  # source i: its tensor's rows at the sampled positions into its buffer
+    r = tl.program_id(
+        1
+    )  # row b * P + p of this micro-batch's rows; written to row at[r] of the buffer
+    src = tl.load(tab + i).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.bfloat16))
+    dst = tl.load(tab + n + i).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.bfloat16))
+    pos = tl.load(idx + r % P)
+    row = tl.load(at + r)
+    offs = tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    for c in range(0, D, BLOCK):
+        m = c + offs < D
+        tl.store(
+            dst + row * D + c + offs,
+            tl.load(src + (r // P) * s_b + pos * s_t + c + offs, mask=m),
+            mask=m,
+        )
+
+
+@torch.library.custom_op("toner_marin::capture_rows", mutates_args=("bufs",))
+def capture_rows(
+    srcs: list[torch.Tensor], bufs: list[torch.Tensor], at: torch.Tensor, idx: torch.Tensor
+) -> None:
+    """bufs[i][at[b P + p]] = srcs[i][b, idx[p]] for bf16 inputs srcs[i] (B, T, D_i) and rows buffers (rows, D_i)."""
+    P = idx.numel()
+    for D in sorted({s.size(-1) for s in srcs}):
+        sel = [i for i, s in enumerate(srcs) if s.size(-1) == D]
+        s0 = srcs[sel[0]]
+        assert (
+            all(
+                srcs[i].dtype == torch.bfloat16
+                and srcs[i].stride() == s0.stride()
+                and bufs[i].is_contiguous()
+                for i in sel
+            )
+            and s0.stride(-1) == 1
+        )
+        tab = torch.tensor(
+            [srcs[i].data_ptr() for i in sel] + [bufs[i].data_ptr() for i in sel], dtype=torch.int64
+        )
+        tab = tab.pin_memory().to(at.device, non_blocking=True)
+        _gather_rows[(len(sel), s0.size(0) * P)](
+            tab, len(sel), at, idx, P, D, s0.stride(0), s0.stride(1), BLOCK=512
+        )
+
+
+@capture_rows.register_fake
+def _(srcs, bufs, at, idx):
+    return None
+
+
+# Recompute sampled RMSNorm and SwiGLU rows without materializing full intermediate inputs.
+@triton.jit
+def _norm_rows(tab, n, at, idx, P, D: tl.constexpr, s_b, s_t, eps, BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
+    i = tl.program_id(0)
+    r = tl.program_id(1)
+    src = tl.load(tab + i).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.bfloat16))
+    w = tl.load(tab + n + i).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.float32))
+    dst = tl.load(tab + 2 * n + i).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.bfloat16))
+    pos = tl.load(idx + r % P)
+    row = tl.load(at + r)
+    offs = tl.arange(0, BLOCK)  # the whole row (BLOCK = D rounded up to a power of two)
+    m = offs < D
+    x = tl.load(src + (r // P) * s_b + pos * s_t + offs, mask=m, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
+    out = (x * tl.math.rsqrt(tl.sum(x * x, 0) / D + eps)).to(tl.bfloat16)
+    h = tl.load(w + offs, mask=m, other=0.0).to(tl.bfloat16).to(tl.float32) * out.to(tl.float32)
+    tl.store(dst + row * D + offs, h.to(tl.bfloat16), mask=m)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _silu_mul_rows(tab, n, at, idx, P, D, s_b, s_t, BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
+    i = tl.program_id(0)
+    r = tl.program_id(1)
+    g = tl.load(tab + i).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.bfloat16))
+    u = tl.load(tab + n + i).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.bfloat16))
+    dst = tl.load(tab + 2 * n + i).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.bfloat16))
+    pos = tl.load(idx + r % P)
+    row = tl.load(at + r)
+    offs = tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    base = (r // P) * s_b + pos * s_t
+    for c in range(0, D, BLOCK):
+        m = c + offs < D
+        gv = tl.load(g + base + c + offs, mask=m).to(tl.float32)
+        uv = tl.load(u + base + c + offs, mask=m).to(tl.float32)
+        # Match the compiled SwiGLU input: FP32 arithmetic, then one BF16 rounding.
+        tl.store(
+            dst + row * D + c + offs,
+            (gv * (1.0 / (1.0 + tl.exp(-gv))) * uv).to(tl.bfloat16),
+            mask=m,
+        )
+
+
+_TABLES = {}  # capture_recomputed's device pointer tables by their content: the activations' addresses repeat across
+# micro-batches (the caching allocator), so in steady state no table is built or copied, and the checks run once
+
+
+@torch.library.custom_op("toner_marin::capture_recomputed", mutates_args=("bufs",))
+def capture_recomputed(
+    xs: list[torch.Tensor],
+    attn_out: list[torch.Tensor],
+    xmid: list[torch.Tensor],
+    gs: list[torch.Tensor],
+    us: list[torch.Tensor],
+    w1: list[torch.Tensor],
+    w2: list[torch.Tensor],
+    bufs: list[torch.Tensor],
+    at: torch.Tensor,
+    idx: torch.Tensor,
+    eps: float,
+) -> None:
+    """Per layer l (bufs in blocks of 4: attn, o, mlp, down): norm(ln1, x) | a | norm(ln2, x_mid) | silu(g) * u at the
+    sampled rows into the rows buffers. All inputs bf16 (B, T, D), the norm weights f32."""
+    P, L, dev = idx.numel(), len(xs), at.device
+    x0, g0 = xs[0], gs[0]
+    B, D = x0.size(0), x0.size(-1)
+    b_attn, b_o, b_mlp, b_down = bufs[0::4], bufs[1::4], bufs[2::4], bufs[3::4]
+    cols = (
+        xs,
+        w1,
+        b_attn,
+        xmid,
+        w2,
+        b_mlp,
+        attn_out,
+        b_o,
+        gs,
+        us,
+        b_down,
+    )  # the kernels' tables, in this order
+    key = tuple(t.data_ptr() for col in cols for t in col)
+    tab = _TABLES.get(key)
+    if tab is None:
+        assert all(
+            t.dtype == torch.bfloat16 and t.stride() == x0.stride() for t in xs + attn_out + xmid
+        )
+        assert (
+            all(t.dtype == torch.bfloat16 and t.stride() == g0.stride() for t in gs + us)
+            and x0.stride(-1) == 1
+        )
+        if len(_TABLES) >= 64:  # addresses that keep changing: keep the cache bounded
+            _TABLES.clear()
+        tab = _TABLES[key] = (
+            torch.tensor(key, dtype=torch.int64).pin_memory().to(dev, non_blocking=True)
+        )
+    NB = triton.next_power_of_2(D)
+    _norm_rows[(L, B * P)](tab[0:], L, at, idx, P, D, x0.stride(0), x0.stride(1), eps, BLOCK=NB)
+    _norm_rows[(L, B * P)](
+        tab[3 * L :], L, at, idx, P, D, x0.stride(0), x0.stride(1), eps, BLOCK=NB
+    )
+    _gather_rows[(L, B * P)](tab[6 * L :], L, at, idx, P, D, x0.stride(0), x0.stride(1), BLOCK=512)
+    _silu_mul_rows[(L, B * P)](
+        tab[8 * L :], L, at, idx, P, g0.size(-1), g0.stride(0), g0.stride(1), BLOCK=512
+    )
+
+
+@capture_recomputed.register_fake
+def _(xs, attn_out, xmid, gs, us, w1, w2, bufs, at, idx, eps):
+    return None
+
+
+# Only cu[:n_docs + 1] and the true max length reach the kernel, so its grid stays tight; both are read from the CPU
+# tensor inside the op, so there is no GPU sync and nothing for torch.compile to specialize on.
+ATTN_HOOK = None  # capture_codegen.Context.attn: sees each attention output here, inside the opaque op (no graph change)
+
+
+@torch.library.custom_op("toner_marin::doc_attn", mutates_args=())
+def doc_attn(
+    q: torch.Tensor, k: torch.Tensor, v: torch.Tensor, cu: torch.Tensor, meta: torch.Tensor
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    n, mx = meta.tolist()
+    c = cu[: n + 1]
+    out, lse, _, _, _ = torch.ops.aten._flash_attention_forward(
+        q, k, v, c, c, mx, mx, 0.0, True, return_debug_mask=False
+    )
+    if ATTN_HOOK is not None:
+        ATTN_HOOK(out)
+    return out, lse
+
+
+@doc_attn.register_fake
+def _(q, k, v, cu, meta):
+    return torch.empty_like(q), q.new_empty((q.size(1), q.size(0)), dtype=torch.float32)
+
+
+@torch.library.custom_op("toner_marin::doc_attn_bwd", mutates_args=())
+def doc_attn_bwd(
+    dout: torch.Tensor,
+    q: torch.Tensor,
+    k: torch.Tensor,
+    v: torch.Tensor,
+    out: torch.Tensor,
+    lse: torch.Tensor,
+    cu: torch.Tensor,
+    meta: torch.Tensor,
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    n, mx = meta.tolist()
+    c = cu[: n + 1]
+    rng = torch.zeros(2, dtype=torch.uint64, device=q.device)
+    dq, dk, dv = torch.ops.aten._flash_attention_backward(
+        dout.contiguous(),
+        q,
+        k,
+        v,
+        out,
+        lse,
+        c,
+        c,
+        mx,
+        mx,
+        0.0,
+        True,
+        rng,
+        torch.empty(0, device=q.device),
+    )
+    return dq, dk, dv
+
+
+@doc_attn_bwd.register_fake
+def _(dout, q, k, v, out, lse, cu, meta):
+    return torch.empty_like(q), torch.empty_like(k), torch.empty_like(v)
+
+
+def _attn_setup(ctx, inputs, output):
+    q, k, v, cu, meta = inputs
+    ctx.save_for_backward(q, k, v, output[0], output[1], cu, meta)
+
+
+def _attn_backward(ctx, dout, dlse):
+    q, k, v, out, lse, cu, meta = ctx.saved_tensors
+    dq, dk, dv = doc_attn_bwd(dout, q, k, v, out, lse, cu, meta)
+    return dq, dk, dv, None, None
+
+
+doc_attn.register_autograd(_attn_backward, setup_context=_attn_setup)

+
+def build_optimizers(model, config, *, rows_total, world, rank, device):
+    o = config["optimizer"]
+    named = dict(model.named_parameters())
+    matrices = [p for n, p in named.items() if n.startswith("body.blocks.") and p.ndim == 2]
+    matrix_ids = {id(p) for p in matrices}
+    rest = [p for p in named.values() if id(p) not in matrix_ids]
+    head = model.head.weight
+    other = [p for p in rest if p is not head]
+    fast = None
+    if o["name"] in ("muont", "adamt"):
+        from toner.fast import roots
+        from toner.fast.engine import FastTonerCore
+
+        if config["statistics"]["damping"] != roots.EPS:
+            raise ValueError("This recorded fast backend requires damping=0.001")
+        fast = FastTonerCore(
+            list(model.body.blocks),
+            named,
+            o["name"],
+            hid=config["model"]["hidden"],
+            mlp=config["model"]["mlp"],
+            rows_total=rows_total,
+            args=fast_arguments(config),
+            world=world,
+            rank=rank,
+            device=device,
+        )

+    elif o["name"] == "muon":
+        from toner.fast.muon import Muon
+
+        optimizers = [
+            Muon(
+                matrices,
+                lr=o["lr"],
+                momentum=o["momentum"],
+                nesterov=o["nesterov"],
+                ns_steps=o["ns_steps"],
+                eps=o["ns_eps"],
+                weight_decay=o["weight_decay"],
+                ns_mode=o["ns_mode"],
+                batched=o.get("batched", True),
+                distributed=o.get("distributed", True) and world > 1,
+            )
+        ]
+    elif o["name"] == "adamw":
+        optimizers = []
+    else:
+        raise ValueError(o["name"])
+    groups = [
+        {"params": [head], "weight_decay": o["head_weight_decay"]},
+        {"params": other, "weight_decay": 0.0},
+    ]
+    if o["name"] == "adamw":
+        groups.insert(0, {"params": matrices, "weight_decay": o["weight_decay"]})
+    auxiliary = torch.optim.AdamW(
+        groups, lr=o["auxiliary_lr"], betas=tuple(o["betas"]), eps=o["eps"], fused=True
+    )
+    optimizers.append(auxiliary)
+    for optimizer in optimizers:
+        for group in optimizer.param_groups:
+            group["base_lr"] = o["auxiliary_lr"] if optimizer is auxiliary else o["lr"]
+    clip_parameters = (
+        rest
+        if o["name"] in ("muon", "muont")
+        else [
+            p
+            for optimizer in optimizers
+            for group in optimizer.param_groups
+            for p in group["params"]
+        ]
+    )
+    return optimizers, fast, clip_parameters
+
+
+@torch.no_grad()
+def clip_gradients(parameters, max_norm):
+    """The recorded global-norm clipping rule, with no additive epsilon."""
+    grads = [p.grad for p in parameters if p.grad is not None]
+    if not max_norm or not grads:
+        return
+    total = torch.linalg.vector_norm(torch.stack(torch._foreach_norm(grads)))
+    scale = torch.where(total < max_norm, 1.0, max_norm / total)
+    torch._foreach_mul_(grads, scale)

+"""Prepare the fixed document prefixes used by the PyTorch Marin comparisons."""
+
+import argparse
+import gzip
+import hashlib
+import io
+import json
+import multiprocessing as mp
+import os
+import time
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import numpy as np
+
+TOK = None
+
+
+def init_worker(tokenizer, revision):
+    global TOK
+    os.environ.setdefault("TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM", "false")
+    from transformers import AutoTokenizer
+
+    TOK = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(tokenizer, revision=revision)
+
+
+def encode(texts):
+    ids = TOK(
+        [t + " " + TOK.eos_token for t in texts],
+        add_special_tokens=True,
+        return_attention_mask=False,
+    )["input_ids"]
+    return [np.asarray(x, dtype="<u4") for x in ids]
+
+
+def iter_texts(repo, rev, path):
+    """Yield document texts from a dataset file, streaming (stop early by closing the generator)."""
+    from urllib.parse import quote
+
+    import requests
+
+    url = f"https://huggingface.co/datasets/{repo}/resolve/{rev}/{quote(path)}"  # e.g. "val_09_c#.jsonl.gz" needs %23
+    from huggingface_hub import get_token
+
+    token = get_token()
+    hdr = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"} if token else {}
+    if path.endswith(".parquet"):
+        import pyarrow.parquet as pq
+        from huggingface_hub import HfFileSystem
+
+        fs = HfFileSystem()
+        with fs.open(f"datasets/{repo}@{rev}/{path}", "rb", block_size=8 << 20) as fh:
+            pf = pq.ParquetFile(fh)
+            for batch in pf.iter_batches(columns=["content"], batch_size=256):
+                for t in batch.column(0).to_pylist():
+                    if t:
+                        yield t
+        return
+    with requests.get(url, headers=hdr, stream=True, timeout=120) as r:
+        r.raise_for_status()
+        r.raw.decode_content = False
+        if path.endswith(".zst"):
+            import zstandard
+
+            raw = zstandard.ZstdDecompressor(max_window_size=2**31).stream_reader(r.raw)
+        elif path.endswith(".gz"):
+            raw = gzip.GzipFile(fileobj=r.raw)
+        else:
+            raw = r.raw
+        for line in io.TextIOWrapper(raw, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"):
+            if line.strip():
+                t = json.loads(line).get("text")
+                if t:
+                    yield t
+
+
+def checksum(path):
+    digest = hashlib.sha256()
+    with path.open("rb") as stream:
+        for block in iter(lambda: stream.read(8 << 20), b""):
+            digest.update(block)
+    return digest.hexdigest()
+
+
+def verify_file(path, record):
+    if not path.exists() or path.stat().st_size != record["tokens"] * 4:
+        return False
+    receipt = path.with_suffix(".bin.json")
+    if receipt.exists():
+        metadata = json.loads(receipt.read_text())
+        return (metadata.get("tokens"), metadata.get("docs"), metadata.get("sha256")) == (
+            record["tokens"],
+            record["docs"],
+            checksum(path),
+        )
+    if record["tokens"] == 0:
+        return record["docs"] == 0
+    # Counts catch truncation and tokenizer mismatches; they are not content hashes.
+    values = np.memmap(path, mode="r", dtype="<u4")
+    documents = sum(
+        int(np.count_nonzero(values[i : i + 1_000_000] == 128001))
+        for i in range(0, len(values), 1_000_000)
+    )
+    return documents == record["docs"]
+
+
+def work(job):
+    record, source, out = job
+    path = Path(out) / record["component"] / record["file"]
+    if path.exists():
+        if not verify_file(path, record):
+            raise ValueError(f"Existing shard does not match expected counts: {path}")
+        return str(path)
+    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    tmp = path.with_suffix(".bin.tmp")
+    for attempt in range(4):
+        try:
+            got, docs, buf = 0, 0, []
+            with tmp.open("wb") as fh:
+                for text in iter_texts(source["repo"], source["revision"], record["path"]):
+                    buf.append(text)
+                    if len(buf) == 64:
+                        for ids in encode(buf):
+                            ids.tofile(fh)
+                            got += len(ids)
+                            docs += 1
+                        buf = []
+                        if record["quota"] is not None and got >= record["quota"]:
+                            break
+                if buf and (record["quota"] is None or got < record["quota"]):
+                    for ids in encode(buf):
+                        ids.tofile(fh)
+                        got += len(ids)
+                        docs += 1
+            if (got, docs) != (record["tokens"], record["docs"]):
+                raise ValueError(f"Token/document count mismatch for {path}: {got}, {docs}")
+            digest = checksum(tmp)
+            os.replace(tmp, path)
+            path.with_suffix(".bin.json").write_text(
+                json.dumps({"tokens": got, "docs": docs, "sha256": digest}) + "\n"
+            )
+            return str(path)
+        except Exception:
+            tmp.unlink(missing_ok=True)
+            if attempt == 3:
+                raise
+            time.sleep(10 * (attempt + 1))
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--out", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=8)
+    parser.add_argument("--split", choices=["all", "train", "validation"], default="all")
+    parser.add_argument("--check-only", action="store_true")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    if args.workers < 1:
+        parser.error("--workers must be positive")
+    plan = json.loads(Path(__file__).with_name("data_plan.json").read_text())
+    records = [
+        r
+        for r in plan["files"]
+        if args.split == "all"
+        or r["component"].startswith("paloma/") == (args.split == "validation")
+    ]
+    if args.check_only:
+        bad = [
+            str(Path(r["component"]) / r["file"])
+            for r in records
+            if not verify_file(args.out / r["component"] / r["file"], r)
+        ]
+        if bad:
+            raise SystemExit(f"Missing or mismatched shards ({len(bad)}): {bad[:10]}")
+        print(f"Verified token/document counts for {len(records)} shards.")
+        return
+    init_worker(plan["tokenizer"], plan["tokenizer_revision"])
+    jobs = [(r, plan["sources"][r["component"]], str(args.out)) for r in records]
+    with mp.get_context("spawn").Pool(
+        args.workers,
+        initializer=init_worker,
+        initargs=(plan["tokenizer"], plan["tokenizer_revision"]),
+    ) as pool:
+        for count, path in enumerate(pool.imap_unordered(work, jobs), 1):
+            print(f"[{count}/{len(jobs)}] {path}", flush=True)
+    args.out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    (args.out / "data_plan.json").write_text(json.dumps(plan, indent=2) + "\n")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+"""Reproduce the recorded PyTorch Marin configurations with torchrun."""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import math
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def schedule_factor(step, schedule):
+    """Learning-rate multiplier at a zero-based optimizer step."""
+    warm = schedule["warmup_steps"]
+    if warm and step < warm:
+        return step / warm
+    step -= warm
+    stable, decay = schedule["stable_steps"], schedule["decay_steps"]
+    if step < stable or not decay or schedule["kind"] == "constant":
+        return 1.0
+    fraction = min(step - stable, decay) / decay
+    minimum = schedule["min_lr_ratio"]
+    if schedule["kind"] == "linear":
+        return 1.0 + (minimum - 1.0) * fraction
+    if schedule["kind"] == "cosine":
+        return (1.0 - minimum) * 0.5 * (1.0 + math.cos(math.pi * fraction)) + minimum
+    raise ValueError(f"Unknown schedule {schedule['kind']}")
+
+
+def load_config(path):
+    with open(path) as stream:
+        config = json.load(stream)
+    return config
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--config", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--data", type=Path, required=True, help="Prepared uint32 shard directory")
+    parser.add_argument("--out", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--max-steps",
+        type=int,
+        help="Stop early for an execution check; does not alter the schedule",
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    if args.max_steps is not None and args.max_steps <= 0:
+        parser.error("--max-steps must be positive")
+    config = load_config(args.config)
+    if config["engine"] != "pytorch":
+        raise SystemExit(
+            "This point uses native Marin/Levanter. Follow the native-run instructions in the Marin README."
+        )
+    import numpy as np
+    import torch
+    import torch.distributed as dist
+    from torch import nn
+    from torch.nn import functional as F
+
+    from . import head_ce
+    from .data import MarinMixture, eval_sets, pack, validate_data_plan
+    from .model import Model, initialize_model, sample_positions
+    from .optimizer import build_optimizers, clip_gradients
+
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
+        raise SystemExit(
+            "These configurations require CUDA, Triton and document-packed FlashAttention."
+        )
+    rank, world = int(os.environ.get("RANK", "0")), int(os.environ.get("WORLD_SIZE", "1"))
+    local = int(os.environ.get("LOCAL_RANK", "0"))
+    torch.cuda.set_device(local)
+    device = torch.device("cuda", local)
+    m, t, runtime = config["model"], config["training"], config["runtime"]
+    if m["hidden"] % 256:
+        raise ValueError("The recorded LM-head kernels require hidden width divisible by 256")
+    if runtime["attention"] not in ("FA2", "FA3"):
+        raise ValueError("attention must be FA2 or FA3")
+    if runtime["head"] not in ("compiled", "triton"):
+        raise ValueError("head must be compiled or triton")
+    if runtime["compile"] not in (
+        "eager",
+        "default",
+        "reduce-overhead",
+        "max-autotune",
+        "max-autotune-no-cudagraphs",
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("Unsupported torch.compile mode")
+    if runtime["eval_every"] <= 0 or t["steps"] <= 0:
+        raise ValueError("Training steps and evaluation interval must be positive")
+    validate_data_plan(args.data, Path(__file__).parent / config["data"]["manifest"])
+    if world != t["world_size"]:
+        raise SystemExit(f"Config requires {t['world_size']} ranks; received {world}.")
+    if world > 1:
+        dist.init_process_group("nccl", device_id=device)
+    torch.manual_seed(t.get("seed", 0))
+    torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False
+    torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 = False
+    if runtime["attention"] == "FA3":
+        torch.nn.attention.activate_flash_attention_impl("FA3")
+    micro, seq, batch = t["micro_batch_size"], m["sequence_length"], t["global_batch_sequences"]
+    if batch % (world * micro):
+        raise ValueError("Global batch must divide into equal full microbatches")
+    accumulation = batch // (world * micro)
+    capture = config["optimizer"]["name"] in ("muont", "adamt")
+    positions, rows, chunk = None, 0, accumulation
+    if capture:
+        s = config["statistics"]
+        positions = sample_positions(seq, s["head"], s["stride"])
+        rows = micro * len(positions)
+        chunk = config["root"]["chunk"] or accumulation
+        if accumulation % chunk:
+            raise ValueError("Statistic chunks must divide the accumulated microbatches")
+        if runtime["capture"] != "recompute":
+            raise ValueError("This reproduction uses recomputed input-row capture")
+    model = Model(m, positions=positions, row_capacity=chunk * rows, rows_per_microbatch=rows).to(

+    )
+    initialize_model(model, t.get("seed", 0), m["embedding_init_scale"])
+    optimizers, fast, clipping = build_optimizers(
+        model, config, rows_total=accumulation * rows * world, world=world, rank=rank, device=device
